title: When He opens a door
hook: when He opens a door of knowing Him, don't mind how little your deeds are (Hikam 8, paraphrased)
tomorrow: the reed has been crying since page one. what's it saying now?

segments.voice: Yesterday, two voices on seeking: strive, and He guides; or, the seeking itself was given. The wanting is His gift. Today, the last saying of the six.
screen: `THE WANTING IS HIS GIFT.` → `THE LAST SAYING.`

segments.voice: An email says you've been invited. A coach waves you up to the varsity bench. A friend's mother opens the door and says, come in, sit, eat. And sometimes the first feeling isn't joy at all. It's: they've made a mistake. My grades, my record, my prayer habits don't match this door. Should you walk in anyway? Ibn Ata'illah has a sentence for that exact flinch, and today it gets something you can feel in your feet: a doorway.
screen: `YOU'VE BEEN INVITED.` → `THEY'VE MADE A MISTAKE.` → `WALK IN ANYWAY?`

segments.voice: Saying eight of the Hikam, paraphrased: when He opens a door for you to know Him, don't worry that your deeds are few. He opened it only because He wanted to make Himself known to you. Don't you see that the knowing is His gift to you, while your deeds are your gift to Him? And how far apart those two gifts are. Read it slowly and the flinch falls apart. The door was never measured against your record. It was measured against the giver. Your deeds still matter; they're what you carry in. They're just not the key. Now the threshold itself. Sahih Muslim keeps a short prayer for walking into a masjid: O God, open for me the doors of Your mercy. The custom is to step in right foot first, saying those words on the way. Every visit to a masjid starts by standing in a doorway and asking for one to open. On the way out, there's a matching line asking for His bounty. So the threshold is a lesson you can feel underfoot: the step in is small, and what it opens onto is large. That's the whole saying. Don't stand outside the open door counting your deeds. Walk through.
screen: `HIKAM EIGHT: DON'T COUNT DEEDS.` · `HIS GIFT, AND YOURS.` · `OPEN FOR ME THE DOORS.` · `A SMALL STEP, A LARGE ROOM.` · then, large: `WALK THROUGH.`

segments.voice: Stand up and walk slowly to the nearest doorway. Pause at the threshold for one full breath, then step through and take a few unhurried steps on the other side, feeling each foot land. Some Muslims step into a masjid right foot first, asking God to open the doors of His mercy; carry that line through with you, or just the step.
screen: `WALK TO A DOORWAY.` · `ONE BREATH AT THE THRESHOLD.` · `STEP THROUGH.`

segments.voice: When He opens a door: Ibn Ata'illah's eighth saying. The knowing is His gift to you; your deeds are your gift to Him.
